answer: Yes. The subtext enriches the hospital setting rather than feeling forced. Cheerful slogans such as “EVERY BABY IS OUR BABY” and “YOUR NEW BEGINNING” contrast with impersonal care, uncertain identification, and Clara’s pain, suggesting a gap between institutional reassurance and lived experience. Small exchanges—“I was already ready,” followed by “You have to tell them”—also convey the women’s vulnerability and struggle to be heard. These details deepen the atmosphere of alienation and make Clara’s final, disturbing choice resonate beyond the literal baby mix-up.
